questions.question:
A company is designing a multi-account structure in AWS Organizations following the AWS Security Reference Architecture. The company wants to centralize security tooling and logs and keep the management account as restricted as possible.

Which design meets these requirements?

options.text: Store logs in each workload account and grant the security team read access.
Use the management account as the delegated administrator for all security services and store logs there.
Create a Security OU with a Security Tooling account (delegated administrator for security services) and a Log Archive account, and run no workloads in the management account.
Create one account per security service in the root of the organization.

questions.explanation: La SRA recomienda una OU Security con cuentas de Security Tooling y Log Archive, delegar la administración de los servicios de seguridad y minimizar el uso de la cuenta de administración (que no está sujeta a SCP).

questions.question:
A company wants to prevent member accounts from disabling GuardDuty, stopping CloudTrail, or leaving the organization. The security team's automation role (SecurityAutomation) must still be able to manage these services.

Which SCP design meets these requirements?

options.text: Deny guardduty:DeleteDetector, cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and organizations:LeaveOrganization with a condition ArnNotLike aws:PrincipalArn for the SecurityAutomation role ARN.
Deny the actions in an SCP and add an Allow statement for SecurityAutomation in the same SCP.
Allow the actions only for the SecurityAutomation role in an SCP, without any Deny statements.
Deny the actions in an IAM policy attached to every user in each account.

questions.explanation: El patrón es Deny con excepción por aws:PrincipalArn. Un Allow no anula un Deny explícito, y las políticas IAM las podrían cambiar los administradores locales.

questions.question:
An SCP attached to the root denies ec2:RunInstances unless the instance type is t3.micro. A developer with AdministratorAccess in a member account cannot launch an m5.large instance, while the same action succeeds when performed by an AWS service-linked role for Auto Scaling.

Why does the service-linked role succeed?

options.text: Service-linked roles are created in the management account.
AdministratorAccess is not evaluated for Auto Scaling.
SCPs apply only to the IAM console, not to service APIs.
SCPs do not affect service-linked roles.

questions.explanation: Las SCP no restringen a los service-linked roles ni a la cuenta de administración; sí afectan a usuarios, roles y root de las cuentas miembro.

questions.question:
A company replaced the default FullAWSAccess SCP on an OU with an SCP that allows only s3:*, ec2:*, and cloudwatch:*. Accounts in a child OU can no longer use AWS Lambda, although the child OU has FullAWSAccess attached.

What is the reason?

options.text: Child OUs inherit only Deny statements, not Allow statements.
Lambda requires an SCP attached directly to the account.
With an allow-list strategy, an action must be allowed by an SCP at every level from the root to the account; the parent OU does not allow Lambda.
FullAWSAccess cannot be attached to child OUs.

questions.explanation: Para que una acción esté permitida, debe estar permitida en cada nivel de la jerarquía (root, cada OU y la cuenta). El nivel padre restringe a todos sus hijos.

questions.question:
A company must ensure that its S3 buckets, KMS keys, and Secrets Manager secrets in all accounts can never be accessed by principals outside its organization, even if a developer writes a permissive resource-based policy. AWS services acting on behalf of the company must continue to work.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer to detect and remove external access every day.
Add an aws:PrincipalOrgID condition to every resource policy with a Config rule.
Attach an SCP that denies access to principals outside the organization.
Attach a resource control policy (RCP) that denies access when aws:PrincipalOrgID does not match the organization, with an exception when aws:PrincipalIsAWSService is true.

questions.explanation: Las RCP limitan los permisos máximos sobre los recursos de las cuentas, aunque la resource policy sea permisiva. Las SCP solo afectan a principales de la organización y no pueden limitar a principales externos.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the difference between SCPs and RCPs?

options.text: SCPs grant permissions to principals; RCPs grant permissions to resources.
RCPs apply to all AWS services; SCPs apply only to S3 and KMS.
SCPs limit the maximum permissions of principals in member accounts; RCPs limit the maximum permissions on resources in member accounts, regardless of who makes the request.
RCPs also apply to resources in the management account.

questions.explanation: Ambas son guardrails (no conceden permisos). Las RCP soportan un subconjunto de servicios (como S3, STS, KMS, SQS y Secrets Manager) y, como las SCP, no afectan a la cuenta de administración.

questions.question:
A company must ensure that no account in the organization can make AMIs or EBS snapshots public, and the configuration must persist even if new APIs are introduced that could change these settings.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use an AWS Organizations declarative policy for EC2 that enables image block public access and snapshot block public access.
Use AWS Config rules with automatic remediation.
Use a tag policy on AMIs and snapshots.
Use an SCP that denies ec2:ModifyImageAttribute and ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute.

questions.explanation: Las políticas declarativas fijan la configuración a nivel de servicio, por lo que se mantiene aunque aparezcan nuevas APIs y pueden mostrar mensajes de error personalizados. Una SCP sobre acciones concretas no cubre APIs nuevas.

questions.question:
The security team wants all new EC2 instances in the organization to require IMDSv2 by default, block VPC internet gateway access for specific accounts, and show developers a custom error message when an action is blocked.

Which feature meets these requirements?

options.text: Declarative policies for EC2 in AWS Organizations.
Service Catalog launch constraints.
Security Hub central configuration.
Tag policies.

questions.explanation: Las políticas declarativas de EC2 cubren, entre otros, valores por defecto de IMDS, VPC Block Public Access, consola serie y Allowed AMIs, con mensajes de error personalizados.

questions.question:
A company has 200 member accounts, each with root user credentials (password and MFA) that must be stored and audited. The security team wants to eliminate root credentials in member accounts while still being able to perform root-only tasks when needed.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an IAM user with AdministratorAccess in each account to replace root.
Rotate the root passwords every 90 days with Secrets Manager.
Use an SCP to deny all actions of the root user and keep the credentials in a vault.

Enable centralized root access management in IAM for the organization, delete the root credentials of member accounts, and perform privileged tasks through sts:AssumeRoot from the management or delegated administrator account.

questions.explanation: La gestión centralizada de root permite eliminar las credenciales de root de las cuentas miembro (y crear cuentas nuevas sin ellas) y ejecutar tareas privilegiadas con sesiones de root acotadas mediante sts:AssumeRoot.

questions.question:
A developer applied an S3 bucket policy that denies all principals, including administrators. Nobody can now modify or delete the policy.

How can the security team fix this with centralized root access enabled?

options.text: Attach an SCP that allows s3:DeleteBucketPolicy.
Open an AWS Support case to delete the policy.
Use sts:AssumeRoot with the task policy for S3 bucket policy deletion on the member account, then delete the bucket policy.
Use the management account's root user to sign in to the member account directly.

questions.explanation: Desbloquear una bucket policy que deniega todo es una tarea de root; con AssumeRoot se obtiene una sesión de root limitada a esa tarea. Una SCP no concede permisos.

questions.question:
A company uses AWS Control Tower. The security team wants to prevent the creation of non-compliant resources before they are deployed through CloudFormation, rather than detecting them afterwards.

Which type of control should the team enable?

options.text: Elective controls implemented with Security Hub.
Preventive controls implemented with tag policies.
Proactive controls, which are implemented with CloudFormation hooks.
Detective controls implemented with AWS Config rules.

questions.explanation: Control Tower ofrece controles preventivos (SCP/RCP), detectivos (Config) y proactivos (hooks de CloudFormation que evalúan los recursos antes del despliegue).

questions.question:
An administrator modified an SCP that AWS Control Tower created on a registered OU. Control Tower now reports drift.

What should the administrator do?

options.text: Repair the landing zone or re-register the OU from Control Tower, and implement custom guardrails as separate SCPs or through Control Tower instead of editing managed SCPs.
Move all accounts to the root of the organization.
Ignore the drift, because Control Tower fixes it automatically every hour.
Delete Control Tower and re-create the organization.

questions.explanation: Modificar recursos administrados por Control Tower genera drift; se corrige reparando o re-registrando. Las restricciones propias deben ir en políticas propias.

questions.question:
A company wants to provision new accounts with a standard baseline (VPC configuration, IAM roles, and security services) through a Terraform-based GitOps workflow integrated with AWS Control Tower.

Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: AWS Service Catalog without Control Tower.
CloudFormation StackSets with self-managed permissions only.
AWS Control Tower Account Factory for Terraform (AFT).
AWS Organizations tag policies.

questions.explanation: AFT crea y personaliza cuentas de Control Tower mediante un pipeline de Terraform.

questions.question:
The finance team requires that every EC2 instance and EBS volume be created with a CostCenter tag, and that the tag values follow a standard list with consistent capitalization.

Which combination meets these requirements?

options.text: Use only a tag policy, which prevents the creation of untagged resources.
Use AWS Config to add missing tags after the resources are created.
Use only an SCP that lists the allowed values for all tags.

Use a tag policy to standardize the key and allowed values (with enforcement for the resource types), and an SCP that denies ec2:RunInstances and ec2:CreateVolume when aws:RequestTag/CostCenter is null.

questions.explanation: Las tag policies estandarizan claves y valores y pueden bloquear valores no conformes, pero no exigen que el tag exista; para eso se usa una SCP con aws:RequestTag.

questions.question:
A company must ensure that a baseline AWS WAF web ACL with AWS managed rules is applied to every Application Load Balancer and API Gateway stage in all current and future accounts, while application teams can add their own rules.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an SCP that requires a web ACL on each ALB.
Create an AWS Firewall Manager WAF policy with first and last rule groups and automatic remediation, scoped to the organization.
Create a CloudFormation StackSet that deploys a web ACL to each account.
Use AWS Config to detect ALBs without a web ACL and notify the teams.

questions.explanation: Firewall Manager aplica las políticas de WAF a recursos actuales y nuevos; los grupos de reglas first/last dejan espacio para las reglas de cada equipo.

questions.question:
A security engineer tries to configure AWS Firewall Manager, but the setup fails in several accounts.

Which prerequisites must be met? (Choose the MOST complete option.)

options.text: Each account must have its own Firewall Manager administrator.
The accounts must be in AWS Organizations, a Firewall Manager administrator account must be designated, and AWS Config must be enabled in the accounts and Regions.
Only AWS Shield Advanced must be enabled in the management account.
GuardDuty must be enabled in every account.

questions.explanation: Firewall Manager requiere Organizations, una cuenta administradora y AWS Config habilitado para descubrir recursos.

questions.question:
The security team wants to detect and automatically remove security group rules that allow 0.0.0.0/0 on administrative ports across all accounts.

Which Firewall Manager policy type should be used?

options.text: A security group content audit policy with automatic remediation.
A Network Firewall policy.
A security group common policy.
A Shield Advanced policy.

questions.explanation: Las políticas de auditoría de contenido de security groups revisan y pueden remediar reglas no permitidas. Las políticas common aplican security groups estándar a los recursos.

questions.question:
Developers deploy infrastructure with CloudFormation. The security team wants templates to be validated in the CI pipeline against rules such as "S3 buckets must have encryption and versioning" before deployment, using a policy-as-code language.

Which tool should the team use?

options.text: CloudFormation drift detection.
IAM Access Analyzer policy validation.
AWS Config conformance packs.
AWS CloudFormation Guard (cfn-guard) with custom rules in the pipeline.

questions.explanation: cfn-guard evalúa plantillas contra reglas declarativas antes del despliegue. Config y drift detection evalúan después.

questions.question:
A CloudFormation stack contains a production database. The security team must prevent stack updates from replacing or deleting the database, while allowing other resources in the stack to be updated.

What should the security engineer configure?

options.text: A stack policy that denies Update:Replace and Update:Delete on the database logical resource, plus a DeletionPolicy of Retain or Snapshot.
Drift detection on the stack.
Termination protection on the stack only.
An SCP that denies cloudformation:UpdateStack.

questions.explanation: Una stack policy protege recursos concretos durante las actualizaciones; DeletionPolicy conserva el recurso si se elimina. La termination protection solo impide borrar el stack completo.

questions.question:
Developers must deploy CloudFormation stacks that create IAM roles, but they must not have IAM permissions themselves.

Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Run CloudFormation with the root user.
Use a CloudFormation service role with the required IAM permissions and allow developers only iam:PassRole for that role and the CloudFormation actions.
Use stack policies to grant IAM permissions.
Grant developers iam:* and rely on code reviews.

questions.explanation: Con un service role, CloudFormation actúa con los permisos del rol, y el desarrollador solo necesita pasarlo (iam:PassRole). Así se separan los permisos del usuario de los del despliegue.

questions.question:
Application teams must be able to launch approved, pre-configured EMR clusters without having permissions to create EMR, EC2, or IAM resources directly.

Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Use an SCP that allows EMR only through the console.
Share the CloudFormation template through AWS RAM.
Grant the teams AdministratorAccess and monitor with CloudTrail.
Publish the EMR template as an AWS Service Catalog product in a portfolio with a launch constraint that specifies an IAM role with the required permissions.

questions.explanation: Con una launch constraint, Service Catalog lanza el producto con el rol indicado; los usuarios finales solo necesitan permisos para usar el catálogo.

questions.question:
A networking account owns the VPCs. Workload accounts must launch resources into centrally managed subnets without managing their own VPCs.

Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Copy the VPC to each account with CloudFormation StackSets.
Share the subnets with the workload accounts using AWS RAM (VPC sharing).
Use a Service Catalog product for each subnet.
Create VPC peering between each workload account and the networking account.

questions.explanation: Con VPC sharing, la cuenta de red comparte subredes por RAM; los participantes lanzan recursos en ellas, pero no pueden modificar la VPC.

questions.question:
The security team must answer ad hoc questions such as "Which EC2 instances in all accounts and Regions are running a specific AMI?" using the current configuration state.

Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Run DescribeInstances in each account and Region with a script.
Query CloudTrail Lake for RunInstances events.
Use the Security Hub CSPM summary dashboard.
Use AWS Config advanced queries (SQL) against a Config aggregator.

questions.explanation: Las advanced queries de Config consultan el estado actual de configuración con SQL, incluso a través de un aggregator multicuenta y multirregión.

questions.question:
The security team wants to write a custom AWS Config rule that checks a configuration property, without writing or maintaining a Lambda function.

Which option meets this requirement?

options.text: A Config custom policy rule written in AWS CloudFormation Guard syntax.
A Security Hub automation rule.
A Config custom Lambda rule.
An EventBridge rule with a CloudWatch alarm.

questions.explanation: Las custom policy rules usan sintaxis de Guard y no requieren Lambda; las custom Lambda rules sí requieren código.

questions.question:
A company uses Security Hub CSPM with a delegated administrator. The security team wants different standards and controls for production and sandbox OUs, configured centrally and applied automatically to new accounts.

What should the security engineer use?

options.text: Enable standards manually in each account.
Create a separate delegated administrator for each OU.
Use an SCP that enables standards per OU.
Security Hub central configuration with configuration policies associated with each OU.

questions.explanation: La configuración central permite definir políticas (servicio, estándares y controles) y asociarlas a OUs o cuentas, heredándose a las cuentas nuevas.

questions.question:
A company must demonstrate alignment with PCI DSS for a set of accounts and continuously evaluate their AWS configuration against the relevant controls.

Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Download the AWS PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance from AWS Artifact only.
Use the Well-Architected Tool with the PCI lens.
Enable GuardDuty in those accounts.
Enable the PCI DSS standard in Security Hub CSPM for those accounts and review the control status.

questions.explanation: El estándar PCI DSS de Security Hub CSPM evalúa continuamente tus recursos. El AOC de Artifact demuestra el cumplimiento de AWS, no el tuyo (modelo de responsabilidad compartida).

questions.question:
An external auditor requests AWS's SOC 2 Type II report for the company's annual audit.

Where should the security engineer obtain it?

options.text: AWS Config conformance packs.
AWS Trusted Advisor.
AWS Security Hub CSPM.
AWS Artifact, after accepting the applicable terms.

questions.explanation: Artifact proporciona los informes de cumplimiento de AWS (SOC, ISO, PCI) y los acuerdos.

questions.question:
A healthcare company must accept the HIPAA Business Associate Addendum (BAA) for all current and future accounts in its organization.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Accept the BAA in each account individually.
Accept the BAA as an organization agreement in AWS Artifact from the management account.
Request the BAA from AWS Support for each new account.
Accept the BAA in the security tooling account.

questions.explanation: Un acuerdo de organización aceptado desde la cuenta de administración cubre todas las cuentas actuales y futuras.

questions.question:
The security team reviewed a critical workload against the Security pillar and fixed several high-risk issues. Management wants evidence of the improvement over time.

What should the team use?

options.text: AWS Well-Architected Tool milestones taken before and after the improvements.
Security Hub CSPM automation rules.
AWS Artifact reports.
AWS Config conformance pack history.

questions.explanation: Los milestones de la Well-Architected Tool capturan el estado de la revisión para comparar el progreso.

questions.question: Which statements about SCPs are correct? (Select THREE.)

options.text: SCPs affect the root user of member accounts
SCPs affect service-linked roles
SCPs apply to principals outside the organization that access your resources
An explicit Allow in an SCP overrides an explicit Deny in an IAM policy
SCPs do not affect the management account
SCPs never grant permissions

questions.explanation: Las SCP son límites máximos para principales de cuentas miembro (incluido root), no aplican a la cuenta de administración ni a service-linked roles, y no afectan a principales externos (para eso existen las RCP).

questions.question: Which tasks still require root user credentials or a root session (for example, through sts:AssumeRoot)? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enabling GuardDuty
Unlocking an SQS queue policy that denies all principals
Creating an IAM role
Deleting an S3 bucket policy that denies all principals
Changing an EC2 instance type

questions.explanation: Algunas tareas solo las puede hacer root, como eliminar políticas de bucket o de cola que deniegan a todos; AssumeRoot permite hacerlas sin credenciales permanentes de root.

questions.question: Order the steps to set up centralized security services in a new organization.

options.text: Create the Security OU with the Security Tooling and Log Archive accounts
Designate the Security Tooling account as delegated administrator for the security services
Enable auto-enable for member accounts in each security service
Apply SCPs that prevent member accounts from disabling the services

questions.explanation: Primero la estructura, luego la delegación, la activación automática y finalmente los guardrails que protegen la configuración.

questions.question: Order the stages where security controls apply in an infrastructure-as-code workflow, from earliest to latest.

options.text: Policy-as-code checks on templates in the CI pipeline (cfn-guard)
Proactive controls that evaluate resources during deployment (CloudFormation hooks)
Preventive guardrails that deny API calls (SCPs and RCPs)
Detective controls on deployed resources (AWS Config rules)

questions.explanation: Cuanto antes se detecta, más barato es corregir; los controles detectivos son la última red de seguridad.

questions.question: Match each AWS Organizations policy type with its purpose.

options.text: Deploy backup plans across accounts
Enforce a service configuration baseline such as EC2 settings
Limit maximum permissions on resources in member accounts
Grant administrator permissions to new accounts
Limit maximum permissions of principals in member accounts
Standardize tag keys and values

questions.explanation: Ningún tipo de política de Organizations concede permisos; todas son controles centralizados.

questions.question: Match each AWS Control Tower control type with its implementation.

options.text: CloudFormation hooks
Amazon GuardDuty findings
AWS Config rules
SCPs and RCPs

questions.explanation: Control Tower implementa sus controles con SCP/RCP, reglas de Config y hooks de CloudFormation.

questions.question:
A company shares an AWS Private CA and transit gateway with all accounts in the organization through AWS RAM. New accounts must receive the shares automatically without accepting invitations.

What should the security engineer do?

options.text: Enable resource sharing with AWS Organizations in RAM and share the resources with the organization or OUs as principals.
Create an SCP that allows ram:AcceptResourceShareInvitation.
Share the resources with each account ID and accept the invitations with a Lambda function.
Copy the resources to each new account with StackSets.

questions.explanation: Con el uso compartido habilitado con Organizations, los recursos compartidos con la organización u OUs llegan sin invitaciones y aplican a las cuentas nuevas.

questions.question:
The security team wants AWS Config rules to evaluate resource configurations before they are created, as part of the deployment process, using the same managed rules that evaluate deployed resources.

Which feature should the team use?

options.text: Config periodic triggers.
Config advanced queries.
Config aggregators.
AWS Config proactive evaluation mode for rules that support it.

questions.explanation: El modo proactivo evalúa la configuración de un recurso antes de desplegarlo (por ejemplo, desde hooks de CloudFormation), con reglas que lo soportan.
